new_material_candidates.name: SOAR — Supervision from Observation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
new_material_candidates.material_reason: SOAR changes the training signal for agentic reinforcement learning by assigning positive advantage to environment-observation tokens according to preceding-action confidence, directly targeting learning of environment dynamics and tool-call consequences.

reference_or_screened.name: EnvScaler
reference_or_screened.relevance: Programmatically synthesizes executable, stateful, tool-interactive environments and scenarios for SFT and RL agent training.
reference_or_screened.reason: Its distinguishing contribution is construction of training environments, scenarios, validation functions, and training infrastructure rather than a uniquely defined decision policy directly comparable under the current N-H1 policy role.

reference_or_screened.name: NOMADD
reference_or_screened.relevance: Post-hoc temporal data-drift mitigation applicable to multiple model families and evaluated on the Drift-Resilient TabPFN benchmark.
reference_or_screened.reason: The work is a preprint and this bounded review did not verify an official executable implementation suitable for governed reproduction.

n_h2_reference_research.name: SOAR
n_h2_reference_research.relevance: Learns agent behavior from action-observation interaction using agentic reinforcement learning.
n_h2_reference_research.reason: The learned decision mechanism is demonstrated inside agentic language-model environments and does not establish transfer into structured-ML and vision families.

n_h2_reference_research.name: DistPFN
n_h2_reference_research.relevance: Provides inference-time label-shift correction for TabPFN-family structured-data models.
n_h2_reference_research.reason: Its mechanism is specific to tabular posterior adjustment and is not a common learned decision mechanism spanning E1, E2, and E3.

stopping_rule.reason: SOAR is a materially distinct, peer-reviewed, executable E1 agentic-RL comparator absent from prior promoted candidate identities.
